title: Asteroid Collision
description:
We are given an array `asteroids` of non-zero integers representing asteroids in a row. The index of each asteroid represents its relative position in space.

For each asteroid, the absolute value represents its **size**, and the sign represents its **direction** (positive means moving to the right, negative means moving to the left). Each asteroid moves at the same speed.

Find out the state of the asteroids after all collisions:
- If two asteroids meet, the smaller one explodes.
- If both are the same size, both explode.
- Two asteroids moving in the same direction (or moving away from each other, i.e. a left-moving asteroid to the left of a right-moving asteroid) will never meet.

Return an array of the surviving asteroids in their original left-to-right order.
hints: A collision can only happen when a right-moving asteroid (positive) is immediately to the left of a left-moving asteroid (negative).
Maintain a stack of surviving asteroids processed from left to right. A new right-moving asteroid can be pushed directly because it cannot collide with anything to its left.

When a left-moving asteroid arrives, repeatedly compare its magnitude with the top of the stack while the top is moving right, popping smaller right-moving asteroids and handling equal-size mutual destruction.

examples.explanation: The 10 and -5 collide resulting in 10. The 5 and 10 never collide.
The 8 and -8 collide and both explode, leaving an empty array.
The 2 and -5 collide resulting in -5. Then 10 and -5 collide resulting in 10.
